findings.description: `refuseUninstalled` refuses any nested package that declares dependencies but has no `node_modules` of its own in the main checkout. That includes npm and yarn-v1 workspace members whose dependencies are hoisted to the root `node_modules`. The gate links that root directory into the checkout (`linkEnvironment(..., '.')`), and those stages used to pass. Now every merge touching such a member is refused as an operator error, and the install command it suggests does not create a member `node_modules`.
findings.body:
**A hoisted workspace member is now refused, though its stages used to run.**

The new check looks for `node_modules` only in the package's own directory:

```ts
if (existsSync(join(repoPath, pkg.dir, GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR))) return;
if (lstatSync(join(checkout, pkg.dir, GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR), { throwIfNoEntry: false })) return;
...
if (Object.keys(declared).length === 0) return;
throw new Error(`${dir} has no ${GATE_ENVIRONMENT_DIR} in the main checkout, ...`);
```

Why that refuses a package that used to pass:

- **Workspace members are nested packages.** `committedPackageDirs` (`src/adapters/git-tree.client.ts:95-98`) treats any directory with a committed `package.json` as a nested package. Its JSDoc, `docs/06-adapters.md:49-51` and ADR 0058 all say this covers workspace members.
- **They run under npm.** An npm or yarn-v1 member has no lockfile of its own, so `packageManager` (`typescript.adapter.ts:170-174`) resolves `npm`, and the stage runs `npm run <stage>` from inside the member.
- **Their dependencies sit at the root.** npm and yarn-v1 hoist them into the root `node_modules`, and usually create no member `node_modules` at all.
- **The gate already links that root.** `linkEnvironment(repoPath, checkoutDir, '.')` links the root's entries, `.bin` included, into `<checkout>/node_modules`. Node resolves upward and `npm run` puts each ancestor's `.bin` on PATH, so before this PR those stages found their tools and passed.

Now every merge that touches such a member throws `nothing was merged. Install it with \`npm --prefix packages/a install\``. Running that installs a separate, non-hoisted tree (plus a stray lockfile) beside the workspace, which is not something the operator should have to do.

The new test covers only a member that has its own `pnpm-lock.yaml`. ADR 0059:108-111 describes a missing install as "a loud failure ... in its stage", and no ADR narrows nested packages to standalone ones.

**Suggested direction:** refuse only when some declared dependency resolves from no `node_modules` between the package and the repo root in the main checkout, for example by walking `dirname(pkg.dir)` up to `'.'`. That keeps the `tools/review` case and stops refusing hoisted members.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/12f2af4eea3e998a1ce39586ff6b0fee99105b5d/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1522-L1541

findings.description: The `?? '--prefix'` fallback on `INSTALL_DIR_FLAG` can never run, because the adapter only resolves pnpm, yarn or npm. Type the map as `Record<'pnpm' | 'yarn' | 'npm', string>` and drop the fallback.
The comment above the new test repeats `refuseUninstalled`'s JSDoc almost word for word. AGENTS.md says to delete a call-site copy of the seam's rationale.
